SETTING (lines 1-3). A finite abelian group is the direct product of two cyclic groups A=[alpha] and B=[beta] with trivial intersection ('A-B=1'). Their orders are (1,A)=a and (1,B)=b. Take pi = alpha^r beta^s, so pi^x = alpha^{rx} beta^{sx}. Its order ('Grad') p is fixed by the Z-module [1, r/a, s/b] = Z*(1/p). Equivalently, p = lcm(a/gcd(a,r), b/gcd(b,s)). Similarly pi_1 = alpha^{r1} beta^{s1} has order p1 with [1, r1/a, s1/b] = Z/p1.

PROBLEM. Find the common elements of the cyclic groups <pi> and <pi_1>, i.e. solve pi^x = pi_1^{x1}. This is equivalent to rx = r1 x1 (mod a) and sx = s1 x1 (mod b). Put rho = r/a, sigma = s/b, rho1 = r1/a, sigma1 = s1/b. The system becomes rho x = rho1 x1 and sigma x = sigma1 x1 (mod 1), with x and x1 integers. This is exactly the system of the previous folio, i.e. intersecting two cyclic subgroups of (Q/Z)^2.

The group <pi, pi_1> has order q, where 1/q generates [D, rho, sigma, rho1, sigma1, 1] and D = rho sigma1 - sigma rho1 = (r s1 - s r1)/(ab).

REDUCTION. Write tau = 1/p and tau1 = 1/p1, so [rho,sigma,1] = Z tau and [rho1,sigma1,1] = Z tau1. Then rho = u tau, sigma = v tau, rho1 = u1 tau1, sigma1 = v1 tau1, with gcd(u,v,p) = gcd(u1,v1,p1) = 1.
- Choose integers h,k,l with h rho1 + k sigma1 + l = tau1. Then h rho + k sigma lies in Z tau, so it equals m tau with m an integer (m = hu + kv).
- Combining the congruences with weights h,k gives m tau x = (tau1 - l) x1 = tau1 x1 (mod 1), i.e. (m/p) x = x1/p1.
- Multiplying by u1 and by v1 gives rho1 x1 = rho1 p1 (m/p) x and sigma1 x1 = sigma1 p1 (m/p) x (mod 1).
- Hence the solvable x are exactly those with x * [1, rho - rho1 m p1/p, sigma - sigma1 m p1/p] contained in Z. Here x1 is then determined mod p1 by x1 = p1 m x/p.

KEY IDENTITIES.
- rho tau1 - rho1 m tau = k D + l rho.
- sigma tau1 - sigma1 m tau = -h D + l sigma.
- Both follow by substituting tau1 = h rho1 + k sigma1 + l and m tau = h rho + k sigma.
- Check: D = (rho - rho1 m p1/p) sigma1 - (sigma - sigma1 m p1/p) rho1 = p1 D (h rho1 + k sigma1 + l) = D.

THE MODULE [D, rho, sigma, rho1, sigma1, 1].
- It equals [D, tau, tau1].
- Multiplying by p p1 gives the integer module [uv1 - vu1, up1, vp1, pu1, pv1, pp1] = [uv1 - vu1, p, p1]. The second equality holds because gcd(u,v,p) = gcd(u1,v1,p1) = 1.
- Call this generator tau2, an integer dividing p and p1. Then [D, ...] = tau tau1 tau2 Z, so q = p2 = p p1/tau2, i.e. tau tau1 tau2 p2 = 1.
- Hence D = tau tau1 tau2 delta with delta an integer. Also (rho - (rho1/tau1) m tau) sigma1/tau1 - (sigma - (sigma1/tau1) m tau) rho1/tau1 = D/tau1 = tau tau2 delta.

THE PRIMED INTEGERS.
- From the key identities, rho - (rho1/tau1) m tau = rho' tau and sigma - (sigma1/tau1) m tau = sigma' tau.
- My explicit check: rho' = k tau2 delta + l u p1 and sigma' = -h tau2 delta + l v p1, both integers.
- Also h rho' + k sigma' = l m/tau1 = l m p1.

CONCLUSIONS.
- [tau1, rho tau1 - rho1 m tau, sigma tau1 - sigma1 m tau] is contained in tau tau1 tau2 Z.
- 'Umgekehrt': D = (rho tau1 - rho1 m tau) v1 - (sigma tau1 - sigma1 m tau) u1, using sigma1/tau1 = v1 and rho1/tau1 = u1, which are integers.
- In the right margin: x tau1 + y(rho tau1 - rho1 m tau) + z(sigma tau1 - sigma1 m tau) = (x + y rho + z sigma) tau1 - (y rho1 + z sigma1) m tau. With y = v1 x1 and z = -u1 x1 this becomes x tau1 + x1 D. So D (and tau1) lie in the module.
- The page breaks off while expressing rho, i.e. while trying to show tau itself lies in the module.

INTENDED RESULT (made explicit by me; it is the content of the previous folio, p = [w,w1,w2]).
- [1, rho - u1 m tau, sigma - v1 m tau] = (tau2/p) Z.
- Hence the admissible x are the multiples of p/tau2.
- |<pi> ∩ <pi_1>| = tau2 = gcd(p, p1, uv1 - vu1), and |<pi, pi_1>| = p p1/tau2.
